missing_evidence: AIS Vessel Kinematics (No authorized vessel transponder feed in target area)
In-Situ Marine Buoy Telemetry (IoT station unmonitored or unconfigured)

positive_factors: Corroborated by 2 distinct observational agents (Oceanographic Agent, SAR Agent).
Cross-agent observations synchronized within high temporal compatibility window (<= 6 hrs).

uncertainty: Contains 2 simulated IoT evidence record(s). Simulated sensor data is isolated and does NOT contribute to real-world incident confidence.
SAR dark backscatter can be caused by natural biogenic slicks, grease ice, or wind shadows (<3 m/s).
alternative_explanations: Riverine stormwater sediment discharge following heavy coastal rainfall.
Shallow water bottom sediment resuspension from tidal currents or wind waves.

nugen_reasoning.observation: Possible water quality anomaly detected in Zone-zone-01 (ID: zone-01) with SAR C-Band (Sigma-0 Backscatter) showing moderate dark slicks and AIS vessel activity within the area.
nugen_reasoning.hypothesis: The anomaly may be caused by natural look-alikes (low-wind zones, biogenic films) or verified hydrocarbon slicks. The AIS vessel activity suggests potential illegal discharge or unauthorized anchoring.

reasoning_chain.claim: Dark slicks detected in Sigma-0 Decibels (dB) with moderate confidence.
Vessel PACIFIC TRADER has had no transponder pings received for 958.2 minutes, indicating potential illegal discharge.

reasoning_chain.consensus: The anomaly may be caused by natural look-alikes or verified hydrocarbon slicks. The AIS vessel activity suggests potential illegal discharge or unauthorized anchoring.

nugen_reasoning.consensus_action: Monitor vessel activity and conduct further investigations to confirm the cause of the dark slicks.
